title: Integral constructibility detected by actual residue reduction
statement:
theorem internal_integral_residue_criterion
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] :
    (∀ K : DerivedCategory (AdicCompletion.Modules l E X),
      constantModelBoundedConstructible (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E) X K ↔
        IsDerivedComplete l E X K ∧
        constantModelBoundedConstructible (DerivedNakayama.quotientRing l E 1) X
          ((AdicCompletion.derivedReduction l E X 0).obj K) ∧
        DerivedCategory.finiteTorAmplitude _
          ((AdicCompletion.derivedReduction l E X 0).obj K)) ∧
    constantModelBoundedConstructible (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E) X =
      (constantModelBoundedConstructible (DerivedNakayama.integerRing l E) X ⊓
        DerivedCategory.finiteTorAmplitude (AdicCompletion.Modules l E X))
All objects and maps use the actual continuous internal coefficient objects; quotient index zero is exponent one.

proof.text: The integral coefficient limit identifies the pulled-back continuous integer ring with the positive quotient limit. Exact section-action and small-site equivalences identify relative tensors, homology, products and scalar quotient maps. Normalize the finite comparison by pure tensors, and the completion comparison by the augmentation, to identify the actual Roos unit with ConstantCompletion.IsComplete after constant scalar restriction.

At residue level, the finite discrete coefficient comparison identifies constant local models and cohomology in the two presentations. Finite Tor amplitude implies boundedness by tensoring with the unit. Conversely the residue is a field by the DVR theorem; exact sheafification of vector spaces and local flatness give finite Tor amplitude for bounded residue complexes. Apply integral_models_stacks to obtain both directions of the first equivalence.

A finite constant module over the integer DVR has a two-term finite free resolution. Pulling it back gives Tor interval [-1,0] locally. On a finite constructible stratification, exact open and closed restriction detects tensor homology, hence the same interval holds globally. Bounded truncation induction gives [a-1,b] for every integral bounded constructible complex. This proves Dbc = Dbc meet finiteTor; the reverse inclusion is immediate.
